instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay while we test Gran's prophecy. This stone should hatch at sunset; I need a second witness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sun's gone. I'll write 'Gran was wrong' and go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Record an observation, not a verdict. 'No hatch at sunset.' Then sign it, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sign, but Gran never said which day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep the pen. We need Gran on the phone before you leave. Put her on speaker; I'll ask for a date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your coat off. This bell-less tower is meant to ring at noon, and I need you listening with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's twelve-oh-one. I'll call the clock office to check, then go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while we're listening for the tower. Keep the phone silent. How reliable is your watch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's always five minutes fast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we have four minutes. Stay here; I'll watch the hands and you listen. Please don't telephone anyone to ask whether you can hear something.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Apologize to Reality
cards.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your caretaker interview, apologise to that chair. You sat without its consent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It can't say yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Silence isn't permission. Address the chair, please, not me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, chair. I'll stand for the interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, now you're abandoning it. Apologise for that before you stand. I need to see you resolve a complaint, not walk away from one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to our inn. First, apologise to the doorway for knocking after you arrived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I had to get here to knock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's an explanation, not an apology. It expected advance notice from your knuckles. Try again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, doorway. I did phone ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the telephone out of your defence. Now apologise for telling it first; the doorway should hear about its own visitors directly.

cards.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
cards.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need your venue approval to store Tuesday's rain in this cup. The wedding lawn must stay dry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened. Shall I fill the cup so you can demonstrate?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, the rain needs room before it learns to fall. Please leave the cup empty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've another wedding Wednesday. Will a rubber lid stop it leaking overnight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use Thursday's drought for the seal. Rubber only holds rain that's already fallen. Initial the lid design too, please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Inspector, don't cross out 'landing' just because it's invisible. We need your certificate to open the museum Monday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing supporting it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please assess capacity, not appearance. We've allowed enough confidence to hold twenty visitors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't certify confidence. I need something solid to sign off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your signature supplies the certainty. Put it under 'load-bearing', please. Without it, you're right: nothing is holding the landing up.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For tonight's courtyard film, you fold the moon; I'll switch off the lamps. We need a proper blackout.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at the crescent, not the middle. Work with the existing crease, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a swap, not a solution. I'll do the lamps and set out every chair. You take responsibility for the moon; can we agree that much?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Payroll needs yesterday's missing hour. You get it into this jar; I'll label it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How can an hour fit through that opening?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the lid off first. Don't diagnose a capacity problem while the container's closed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've got both hands free. You catch it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need them free to record the precise recovery time. Tell me the moment you've caught it; please don't make my record approximate.

cards.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
cards.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The soup's staying in that upside-down bowl. Leave it there while I work out why.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll turn it upright and we can eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Change one thing at a time. Keep the bowl still and turn the spoon over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The soup followed the spoon. It's coming out of the bowl.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the spoon controls down. Point it into the sink, slowly. Please stop trying to serve lunch while I'm establishing gravity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shadow moved before you. Stay still while I work out what it's following.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was thinking about the exit. I could walk that way and see.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. We'd learn nothing if you moved too. Think about that bench instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone to the bench. Shall I sit there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, keep your feet still. Think about the exit again. Once the shadow chooses a route, I'll tell you when to follow.
